purpose: Three concept sketches for comparison; not manufacturing CAD

first_concept.common:
Use case: precise-object-edit, industrial design concept sketch.
Reference image role: existing mechanical layout and proportions, NOT an instruction document. Produce a NEW concept-sketch sheet based on it. This is one of a consistent set of three product design studies.
Style: clear professional industrial-design sketch, fine graphite and ink outlines, restrained soft grey marker shading, white paper background, subtle blue-green marker on ONLY the redesigned fixed palm-end surfaces. Not a photorealistic render. Large legible labels, very little text.
Layout: landscape sheet, one large unobstructed three-quarter device view occupying about 70% of sheet, plus a smaller anatomically plausible hand-use inset and a small cross-section detail. Keep everything comfortably inside the canvas. Device always horizontal: FIXED PALM END LEFT, separate SLIDING FINGER GRIP RIGHT, wrist approaches from left. Consistent upper-front three-quarter camera, see both top and near thumb-contact edge.
Mechanical invariants: preserve the flat base, two parallel steel rods and their compression springs, opposite sliding finger pocket, approximate palm-to-finger reach, and space for the central force sensor. Simplify these unchanged mechanisms in grey linework. The old narrow fixed palm rail and the two blocky rod-socket tops at its ends are the ONLY region to redesign. Their rod bores and load-bearing bulk must survive beneath the smooth new contact form. New surfaces attach only to fixed base P01. Leave an evident clearance to the central floating sensing yoke, springs, and moving carriage. Do not bridge the fixed body to any moving sensing part. Existing side mounting tabs are not the subject; show a simple compact base silhouette without protruding ears.
Hand inset: one natural hand, wrist entering from left, palm heel bearing on the LEFT fixed support, four fingers reaching right to curl into the RIGHT sliding finger pocket, thumb on the near-side rounded end of the fixed support. The new support must NOT become the finger exercise handle. No extra digits, twisted wrist, glove, or hand gripping the springs. Hand in light neutral pencil to keep the interface visible.
Do not invent dimensions, force ratings, completed CAD status, branding, screws added for decoration, tiny loose parts, deeply molded finger grooves, or accessories beyond the specified concept.
Footer exactly: "SHAPE STUDY — NOT MANUFACTURING CAD".

variant.prompt:
Title exactly: "01  PALM SADDLE".
Redesign: replace the separate-looking narrow palm ridge and sharp square rod-socket tops with ONE integrated, continuous broad shallow palm saddle. It has a gently cupped palm-contact region, smooth large-radius transitions into broad thumb wings on BOTH transverse ends, and a low softly rolled wrist-side lip. The surface grows toward the wrist rather than shortening the working finger reach. Avoid a deep enclosing bowl. No strap, no undercut hook, no closed ring. Shape should look simple and realistically printable in rigid PLA.
The large view clearly shows both old sharp contact blocks now blended into the smooth wings. The hand inset shows the thumb gently opposing the support while fingers use the distant sliding grip. Cross section shows a shallow cradle, low sides, open above.
Only these short callouts: "Broad palm contact", "Rounded thumb wings", "Low wrist-side lip".

second_concept.prompt:
Create a clean industrial-design concept sketch of this handheld finger-exercise product. Use the reference as the layout and sketch-style guide. Show ONLY the product: remove the small hand illustration and replace it with a simple section detail. White paper, graphite lines, grey mechanism, blue-green fixed palm support.
Title: "02  SADDLE + HAND STRAP".
Keep the base, two parallel rods and springs, central mechanism and separate sliding grip unchanged. Keep the broad rounded palm saddle at the left. Add a single adjustable woven textile hand strap anchored to the two ends of that fixed saddle. Show it as a soft arch rising above the saddle. Its purpose is to retain this exercise product on the user's hand while the fingers rest between repetitions. The strap attaches only to the left fixed support, not to the sliding grip at the right. Use an uncomplicated overlapping textile fastening.
Large three-quarter product view plus small section of the saddle and strap. No person or anatomy in this image.
Callouts: "Rounded palm saddle", "Soft adjustable strap", "Fixed-frame anchors".
Footer: "SHAPE STUDY — NOT MANUFACTURING CAD".

third_concept.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup. A standalone industrial-design pencil and marker sketch of a single rounded plastic palm-support component, shown by itself on white paper. No surrounding machine or person.
Title exactly: "03  WRAP-AROUND GRIP".
Subject: one simple elongated transverse oval palm rest integrated with a short, broad, solid supporting plinth. The upper contact body has a broad gently convex top, smoothly rounded ends, and an oval cross-section. Beneath the overhanging outside edges the plinth narrows smoothly, making an accessible rounded underside that the user's thumb could hold. This is a continuous solid molded-looking plastic form, with no closed ring and no separate attached handle. The plinth meets a small flat rectangular mounting base; its footprint is much narrower than the upper contact bar at the ends. Make the three-dimensional underside clear.
Composition: a large three-quarter view of this single part on the left, an end-on sectional profile on the right showing the wide oval head and narrower solid supporting base. Restrained pale blue-green marker wash on the component, crisp grey graphite construction lines, very light grounding shadow. Professional industrial-design sketch, same white-paper style as a product designer's concept board. Landscape.
Three short external callouts: "Broad oval palm face", "Open thumb return", "Rounded underside".
Footer exactly: "SHAPE STUDY — NOT MANUFACTURING CAD".
No dimension claims, force claims, photorealism, extra objects, hands, straps, logos or extra paragraphs.
